keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Makololo row). The only land the pages name is the conquered Barotseland: 'By 1845, Sebetwane had conquered Barotseland and became king' (Makololo); the Sebetwane page places the nation 'in what is now southwestern Zambia'. The wider Makololo sphere (Chobe, the Batoka plateau) is not on the pages. Confidence 1.

ledger.note: Around 1840: the Makololo take Barotseland. Sebetwane page: 'around 1840' the group 'struck north again' after the 1838 stay near Victoria Falls; Barotseland page: 'Around 1840, Sebitwane's Makololo entered onto the Plain'; Makololo page: 'By 1845, Sebetwane had conquered Barotseland and became king.' The Makololo moved north from 1823.

sources.title: Barotseland
sources.note: Founded 17th century; Makololo c. 1840-1864; Lewanika 1878-1916 (broken 1884-85); late-19th-century area 390,000 km2; Lochner 1890; Lawley 1898; 1899 Order; losses 1905 (Angola) and 1911 (Caprivi); Northern Rhodesia 1911

sources.title: Makololo
sources.note: Migration from 1823; conquest of Barotseland by 1845; Sebetwane died 1851; Sekeletu; dynasty ended 1864

sources.title: Sebetwane
sources.note: Moved north 1823; Dithubaruba 1826; Okavango 1834; Victoria Falls 1838; around 1840 north again; died 7 July 1851 at Linyati, his capital

notes: Cliopatria has no Makololo row. Pages: Makololo, Sebetwane, Barotseland. Dates: migration north from 1823, defeat at Dithubaruba 1826 by the Ngwaketse, to the Okavango 1834, victory over the Batawana 1835, near Victoria Falls 1838, Lozi plain c. 1840 (pages say c. 1830, 1838, c. 1840, by 1845); Sebetwane died 7 July 1851 at Linyati; succeeded by his daughter Mamochisane, who abdicated for Sekeletu; end 1864. The Linyanti capital is outside Zambia (not drawn); the Western Province stand-in covers only the Barotse Plain. Pre-1840 Makololo state in Botswana (1823-40) held no land the pages bound and is not drawn. Counterpart: lozi-kingdom (this batch). Gazetteer name needed: Linyanti.
